lay_description: Broad group of infections and maternal, newborn, and nutrition-related conditions.
Diseases caused by bacteria, viruses, or parasites that can spread.
Bacterial infection that usually attacks the lungs, known as TB.
Sexually transmitted infections other than HIV.
Bacterial sexually transmitted infection that can spread through the body if untreated.
Common bacterial sexually transmitted infection affecting the genitals.
Bacterial sexually transmitted infection affecting the genitals, throat, or rectum.
Sexually transmitted infection caused by a tiny parasite.
Viral sexually transmitted infection that causes genital sores.
Other sexually transmitted infections not listed separately.
Infection with HIV, which weakens the immune system and can lead to AIDS.
Tuberculosis that develops in people whose immune system is weakened by HIV.
Other illnesses that develop because HIV has weakened the immune system.
Illnesses causing diarrhoea, often from infection, which can lead to dehydration.
Group of childhood infections such as measles, whooping cough, and tetanus.
Contagious lung infection causing violent coughing, also called pertussis.
Serious bacterial infection of the throat and airways.
Highly contagious viral infection causing fever and a rash.
Bacterial infection causing painful muscle stiffness, often after a wound.
Inflammation of the membranes covering the brain and spinal cord.
Inflammation of the brain, usually caused by an infection.
Inflammation of the liver, most often caused by a virus.
Liver infection from hepatitis A virus, usually spread through contaminated food or water.
Liver infection from hepatitis B virus, spread through blood and body fluids.
Liver infection from hepatitis C virus, mainly spread through blood.
Liver infection from hepatitis E virus, usually spread through contaminated water.

Disease spread by mosquito bites, causing fever and chills.
Sleeping sickness, a parasitic infection spread by the tsetse fly.

Parasitic worm infection caught from contaminated fresh water.
Parasitic infection spread by sandfly bites, affecting skin or organs.

Infection from pork tapeworm larvae, which can affect the brain.
Infection from tapeworm larvae that form cysts in the body.
Viral infection spread by mosquitoes, causing fever and body aches.
Bacterial eye infection that can lead to blindness if untreated.
Viral infection spread by mosquitoes, causing fever and jaundice.
Viral infection spread through animal bites, affecting the nervous system.
Infections caused by worms living in the intestines.
Infection from roundworms living in the intestines.
Infection from whipworms living in the large intestine.
Infection from hookworms in the intestines, which can cause anaemia.
Infections from flatworms caught by eating raw or undercooked food.
Long-term bacterial infection of the skin and nerves, also called Hansen's disease.
Other infectious and parasitic diseases not listed separately.
Infections of the airways and lungs.
Infections of the lungs and lower airways, such as pneumonia.
Illness caused by the coronavirus that emerged in 2019.

Infection of the middle ear, common in young children.
Health problems related to pregnancy and childbirth.

Complications in babies who are born too early.

Blood infections and other infections in newborn babies.

Low red blood cell count caused by too little iron.

Long-term diseases that are not passed from person to person.

Cancer of the large bowel, including the colon and rectum.

Cancer of the windpipe, airways, or lungs.
Melanoma and other cancers of the skin.

Common, usually less serious cancers of the skin.
Cancer that starts in the breast.
Cancer of the cervix, the lower part of the womb.

Cancer that starts in the ovaries.

Cancer that starts in the bladder.

Cancer of the thyroid gland in the neck.

Cancer of the blood and bone marrow.

Growths that are not cancer or of uncertain type.

Disorders of hormones, blood, and the immune system.
Inherited blood disorder affecting how the body makes haemoglobin.

Other disorders of hormones, blood, and the immune system.

Long-lasting depression with milder but persistent low mood.

Mental illness affecting thoughts, perceptions, and sense of reality.

Health problems from using other drugs in a harmful way.

Developmental conditions affecting communication and social interaction.

Childhood condition with repeated aggressive or rule-breaking behaviour.
Below-average intellectual ability from an early age, with no known cause.

Loss of memory and thinking ability, including Alzheimer disease.
Disease that gradually affects movement, causing tremor and stiffness.
Condition of the brain that causes repeated seizures.

Recurring headaches, often severe and throbbing.
Ongoing headaches that are not migraines.

Eye disease causing loss of central vision with age.

Sudden inflammation of the kidney's filtering units.

Ongoing pain in the back or neck.

Complete loss of all natural teeth.

Death from traffic crashes on the road.

Death from accidents involving machinery or physical force.
Death caused by natural disasters, such as floods or earthquakes.

Death by suicide or self-inflicted injury.
Death caused by violence from another person.
Death from war, conflict, or legal or police action.
